'''Federico Rodríguez Hertz''' (born December 14, 1973) is an Argentine mathematician working in the United States. He is the Anatole Katok Chair professor of mathematics at [[Penn State University]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://math.psu.edu/dynsys|title=Anatole Katok Center for Dynamical Systems and Geometry {{!}} Department of Mathematics|website=math.psu.edu|access-date=2019-09-11|archive-date=2019-05-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190505211225/https://math.psu.edu/dynsys|url-status=dead}}</ref> Rodriguez Hertz studies [[dynamical system]]s and [[ergodic theory]], which can be used to described [[Chaos theory|chaos's]] behaviors over the large time scale and also has many applications in [[statistical mechanics]], [[number theory]], and [[geometry]].

== Early life and education ==
He is the son of Mariana Frugoni and Adolfo Rodriguez Hertz. He has four siblings, including [[Jana Rodriguez Hertz|Jana]], a mathematician, teacher and researcher.

Rodriguez Hertz studied at the [[Universidad Nacional de Rosario]] in Argentina as an undergraduate student. He moved to Montevideo, Uruguay in 1995, and, unable to continue studies there, he moved in 1996 to Rio de Janeiro where he studied at the graduate school at [[Instituto Nacional de Matemática Pura e Aplicada|IMPA]] and earned a doctoral degree at the IMPA in Brazil in 2001 (with a thesis on "Stable Ergodicity of Toral Automorphisms" under [[Jacob Palis]]).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=53788|title=Federico Rodriguez-Hertz – The Mathematics Genealogy Project|website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu|access-date=2019-09-11}}</ref> His doctoral thesis was published in the Annals of Mathematics and made a breakthrough in this field.<ref name=":1" /> After he received his Ph.D., he moved back to Uruguay, where worked at the National University until moving to [[Pennsylvania State University|Penn State]].

== Work and research ==
Rodriguez Hertz has published research papers in journals including ''[[Annals of Mathematics]]'', ''[[Acta Mathematica]]'', ''[[Journal of the American Mathematical Society]]'', ''[[Inventiones Mathematicae]]'', ''[[Contemporary Mathematics]]'', and ''[[Journal of Modern Dynamics]]''.

The first important contribution of Federico Rodriguez Hertz is his thesis dealing with stable ergodicity,<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last=Hertz|first=Federico|date=2005-07-01|title=Stable ergodicity of certain linear automorphisms of the torus|url=http://annals.math.princeton.edu/2005/162-1/p02|journal=Annals of Mathematics|volume=162|issue=1|pages=65–107|doi=10.4007/annals.2005.162.65|issn=0003-486X|doi-access=free|arxiv=math/0212345}}</ref> which established the tools for proving stable ergodicity of non accessible systems. Then jointly with Jana Rodriguez Hertz, Ali Tahzibi and Raul Ures, Federico Rodriguez Hertz<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Rodriguez Hertz|first1=F.|last2=Rodriguez Hertz|first2=M. A.|last3=Tahzibi|first3=A.|last4=Ures|first4=R.|date=August 2011|title=Uniqueness of SRB Measures for Transitive Diffeomorphisms on Surfaces|journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics|volume=306|issue=1|pages=35–49|doi=10.1007/s00220-011-1275-0|issn=0010-3616|arxiv=1005.4149|bibcode=2011CMaPh.306...35R|s2cid=119600362 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Rodriguez Hertz|first1=F.|last2=Rodriguez Hertz|first2=M. A.|last3=Tahzibi|first3=A.|last4=Ures|first4=R.|date=December 2011|title=New criteria for ergodicity and nonuniform hyperbolicity|journal=Duke Mathematical Journal|volume=160|issue=3|pages=599–629|doi=10.1215/00127094-1444314|issn=0012-7094|arxiv=0907.4539|s2cid=14240460 }}</ref> has proved a series of deep results about the geometry of Hopf brushes. It has been commented that his work "allows one to bring to the spotlight new powerful tools of rigidity theory, in particular topological and geometric methods".<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Dolgopyat|first=Dmitry|date=June 2016|title=The work of Federico Rodriguez Hertz on ergodicity of dynamical systems|journal=Journal of Modern Dynamics|volume=10|issue=2|pages=175–189|doi=10.3934/jmd.2016.10.175|issn=1930-5311|doi-access=free}}</ref> Later, Rodriguez Hertz has researched rigidity theory, which describes the flexibility and motion of sets of rigid bodies. His work in nonuniform-measure rigidity has advanced ergodic theory.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kalinin|first1=Boris|last2=Katok|first2=Anatole|last3=Rodriguez Hertz|first3=Federico|date=2011-07-01|title=Nonuniform measure rigidity|url=http://annals.math.princeton.edu/2011/174-1/p10|journal=Annals of Mathematics|volume=174|issue=1|pages=361–400|doi=10.4007/annals.2011.174.1.10|issn=0003-486X|doi-access=free|arxiv=0803.3094}}</ref> A recent work of Aaron Brown and Federico Rodriguez Hertz<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Brown|first1=Aaron|last2=Hertz|first2=Federico Rodriguez|date=2017-03-07|title=Measure rigidity for random dynamics on surfaces and related skew products|journal=Journal of the American Mathematical Society|volume=30|issue=4|pages=1055–1132|doi=10.1090/jams/877|issn=0894-0347|doi-access=free|arxiv=1406.7201}}</ref> provides a significant generalization of nonuniform-measure rigidity theory. Another very important work of Rodriguez Hertz is on global rigidity of Anosov actions,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Hertz|first=Federico|date=April 2007|title=Global rigidity of certain Abelian actions by toral automorphisms|journal=Journal of Modern Dynamics|volume=1|issue=3|pages=425–442|doi=10.3934/jmd.2007.1.425|issn=1930-5311|doi-access=free|arxiv=math/0609651}}</ref> joint with Zhiren Wang<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Rodriguez Hertz|first1=Federico|last2=Wang|first2=Zhiren|date=October 2014|title=Global rigidity of higher rank abelian Anosov algebraic actions|journal=Inventiones Mathematicae|volume=198|issue=1|pages=165–209|doi=10.1007/s00222-014-0499-y|issn=0020-9910|arxiv=1304.1234|bibcode=2014InMat.198..165R|s2cid=54765968 }}</ref> and joint with Aaron Brown and Zhiren Wang,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Brown|first1=Aaron|last2=Rodriguez Hertz|first2=Federico|last3=Wang|first3=Zhiren|date=2017-11-01|title=Global smooth and topological rigidity of hyperbolic lattice actions|journal=Annals of Mathematics|volume=186|issue=3|pages=913–972|doi=10.4007/annals.2017.186.3.3|issn=0003-486X|arxiv=1512.06720|jstor=26395702|s2cid=96478987 }}</ref> which has been seen as "the crowning achievements in the work on global rigidity of Anosov actions on tori and nilmanifolds".<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Spatzier|first=Ralf|date=June 2016|title=On the work of Rodriguez Hertz on rigidity in dynamics|journal=Journal of Modern Dynamics|volume=10|issue=2|pages=191–207|doi=10.3934/jmd.2016.10.191|issn=1930-5311|bibcode=2016arXiv160600527S|arxiv=1606.00527|s2cid=119121849 }}</ref>

Federico Rodriguez Hertz is an editor of the ''[[Journal of Modern Dynamics]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://aimsciences.org/journal/1930-5311/editorialboard|title=American Institute of Mathematical Sciences|website=aimsciences.org|access-date=2019-09-11}}</ref> He has served as a referee for many distinguished peer-reviewed journals, including [[Annals of Mathematics]] and ''[[Inventiones Mathematicae]]'', and as an evaluator for the Fondo Nacional de Desarrollo Cientifico y Tecnologico, a research foundation promoting science and technology in Chile. He has given invited talks in conferences, workshops and at academic institutions in the United States, Canada, Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay, China, Chile, Poland, Mexico, Germany, Italy, France, Portugal and India.

== Teaching ==
Rodriguez Hertz was a professor of mathematics in the engineering school at the Universidad de la República in Uruguay since 2002. He joined [[Pennsylvania State University|Penn State]]'s [[Eberly College of Science]] Department of Mathematics in 2011 as a professor, and holds the Anatole Katok professorship since 2019.<ref name=":0" />

== Honors and recognition ==
In 2005, Rodriguez Hertz received Premio Roberto Caldeyro Barcia Award from Uruguay's Basic Science Development Program. In 2009, he received an award from the Mathematical Union for Latin America and the Caribbean.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://news.psu.edu/story/467913/2017/05/10/academics/rodr%C3%ADguez-hertz-awarded-faculty-scholar-medal-outstanding|title=Rodríguez Hertz awarded Faculty Scholar Medal for Outstanding Achievement {{!}} Penn State University|website=news.psu.edu|access-date=2019-09-11|archive-date=2018-09-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180907150134/https://news.psu.edu/story/467913/2017/05/10/academics/rodr%C3%ADguez-hertz-awarded-faculty-scholar-medal-outstanding|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2010 he was an invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians in 2010 in Hyderabad, India.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.wias-berlin.de/imu/archive/ICM2010/www.icm2010.in/scientific-program/invited-speakers.html|title=International Congress of Mathematicians 2010, Hyderabad » Invited Speakers|access-date=2019-09-11|archive-date=2022-11-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221116093357/https://www.wias-berlin.de/imu/archive/ICM2010/www.icm2010.in/scientific-program/invited-speakers.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2015 he received the Brin Prize in Dynamical Systems.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://science.psu.edu/clone-michael-brin-prize-in-dynamical-systems|title=Michael Brin Prize in Dynamical Systems|work=Anatole Katok Center For Dynamical Systems And Geometry|publisher=Penn State Eberly College of Science|access-date=2024-04-10}}</ref> In 2017, Rodriguez Hertz has been selected to receive the Penn State Faculty Scholar Medal for Outstanding Achievement in the Physical Sciences. This award was established in 1980 to "recognize scholarly or creative excellence represented by a single contribution or a series of contributions around a coherent theme".<ref name=":2" />
